hero.title: Hormuz Shipping Falls to Seven Vessels as Middle East Crisis Deepens
hero.description: Shipping through the Strait of Hormuz has fallen dramatically as the US–Iran conflict continues, while Houthi forces expand their position around another major global maritime chokepoint.

breaking: 🚢 Strait of Hormuz: only seven vessel transits were recorded on Thursday, far below normal traffic.
🛢️ Brent crude remains above $100 as markets react to continuing Middle East supply and shipping risks.
🇾🇪 Iran-aligned Houthi forces have reached strategic Perim Island near the Bab el-Mandeb shipping route.
🇳🇬 Nigeria's parliament suspends official parliamentary engagements with South Africa over continuing anti-migrant violence.
🇳🇬 Dangote Refinery secures at least 16 million barrels of Nigerian crude for October.
🌍 DR Congo's Ebola outbreak has spread to Sud-Ubangi, becoming the seventh affected province.
🇺🇦 Russian attacks continue in Ukraine as European concern over critical infrastructure grows.
🇺🇸 The United States marks 25 years since the September 11 attacks, with memorial ceremonies across the country.
⛽ US diesel prices remain above $6 per gallon for the first time.
🌐 Oil tanker freight rates reach record highs as Middle East shipping risks increase.

featured.title: Hormuz Traffic Collapses as Global Shipping Faces New Risks
featured.content: Only seven vessels were recorded passing through the Strait of Hormuz on Thursday, compared with a recent 10-day average of 15 and a pre-war daily average of about 125 commercial vessels. The sharp fall illustrates the scale of disruption around one of the world's most important energy corridors. Although diplomatic efforts to improve shipping conditions have emerged, the market remains highly sensitive to further military developments.
featured.imageQuery: Strait of Hormuz tanker shipping oil night

articles.title: Hormuz Shipping Falls to Seven Vessels
articles.content: Data shows that just seven vessels transited the Strait of Hormuz on Thursday. That compares with an average of 15 vessels over the previous 10 days and about 125 commercial vessels per day before the war. The decline is creating serious uncertainty for global oil and commodity supply chains.
articles.imageQuery: Strait of Hormuz commercial vessels tanker

articles.title: Oil Remains Above $100 as Diplomatic Efforts Emerge
articles.content: Brent crude fell from its day's high but remained above $100, while US crude also stayed around the $100 level. Markets reacted positively to reports of possible diplomatic efforts aimed at improving shipping through Hormuz, although there is no confirmed lasting agreement to restore normal traffic.

articles.title: Oil Tanker Freight Rates Hit Record Levels
articles.content: The cost of transporting crude oil has surged to record levels as shipping companies face greater security risks around the Gulf. Rates for very large crude carriers travelling from the Gulf of Oman to China reached around $11.50 per barrel, adding another potential source of inflation for the global economy.

articles.title: Two Global Shipping Chokepoints Face Pressure
articles.content: The disruption is no longer limited to the Strait of Hormuz. Iran-aligned Houthi forces have expanded their control along Yemen's Red Sea coast and reached strategic Perim Island near the Bab el-Mandeb. The development raises concerns about simultaneous pressure on two critical maritime routes.
articles.imageQuery: Bab el Mandeb Red Sea shipping map

articles.title: Nigeria Parliament Suspends South Africa Engagements
articles.content: Nigeria's parliament has suspended official parliamentary visits to South Africa and ordered lawmakers to boycott South African-hosted legislative activities because of continuing anti-migrant violence targeting Nigerians and other African nationals. Nigerian officials say 98 Nigerians have died in mob and hate-related incidents in South Africa since 2022, while 1,695 Nigerians were voluntarily evacuated in 2026.

articles.title: Dangote Secures 16 Million Barrels for October
articles.content: Dangote Refinery has secured at least 16 million barrels of Nigerian crude for October, equivalent to roughly 520,000 barrels per day. The supply represents a significant portion of the refinery's 700,000-barrel-per-day capacity and comes as international crude supplies face disruption.

articles.title: Nigeria's Refining Strategy Gains Importance
articles.content: The continuing global energy disruption highlights the strategic importance of Nigeria's domestic refining capacity. Increased local refining could help reduce dependence on imported petroleum products, while higher international crude prices could also increase export earnings. The challenge will be balancing energy revenues with the cost of fuel and transport for Nigerian consumers.

articles.title: Ebola Outbreak Reaches Seventh Province in DR Congo
articles.content: The Democratic Republic of Congo's Ebola outbreak has spread to Sud-Ubangi, marking the seventh affected province and the first spread into western Congo during this outbreak. Authorities identified the Bundibugyo strain. The response is being complicated by conflict, displacement, population movement and pressure on healthcare workers.

articles.title: Health Authorities Step Up Ebola Response
articles.content: Congo is using the Ervebo vaccine while clinical trials continue for a vaccine targeting the Bundibugyo strain. Health authorities and international partners are monitoring the outbreak closely because movement between affected areas and neighbouring countries could increase the risk of further transmission.

articles.title: European Security Concerns Grow Over Undersea Infrastructure
articles.content: European governments continue to focus on the vulnerability of undersea communication and energy infrastructure. Recent reports of Russian activity around the Arctic have renewed concerns over cables that carry essential international communications and data.
articles.imageQuery: undersea fibre optic cable Europe security

articles.title: Ukraine Faces Continued Russian Attacks
articles.content: Russian attacks continue across Ukraine, with strikes hitting cities and critical infrastructure. The conflict remains a major European security concern, particularly as governments prepare for another difficult winter and assess the resilience of Ukraine's energy system.

articles.title: America Marks 25 Years Since September 11
articles.content: The United States is marking the 25th anniversary of the September 11, 2001 attacks. Memorial ceremonies are taking place across the country to honour the nearly 3,000 people killed when al-Qaida hijackers seized four aircraft and attacked locations in New York, Washington and Pennsylvania.

articles.title: 9/11 Anniversary Brings Reflection on a Quarter Century
articles.content: The 25th anniversary has prompted renewed discussion about the long-term consequences of the attacks, including the wars, counter-terrorism policies and security changes that followed. Families and survivors have continued to call for remembrance without allowing the tragedy to become a source of renewed hatred.

articles.title: Global Shipping Costs Add to Inflation Risks
articles.content: Record oil tanker freight rates are becoming another concern for businesses and consumers. If high shipping costs persist, they could increase the cost of transporting energy and other commodities between regions, adding to inflationary pressure already created by higher fuel prices.
articles.imageQuery: oil tanker shipping business global trade

articles.title: Markets Remain Focused on Middle East Developments
articles.content: Investors remain highly sensitive to developments around Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb. Oil above $100, record tanker rates and uncertainty over supply are forcing markets to reassess inflation, interest rates and the outlook for global economic growth.
articles.imageQuery: global financial markets oil trading screens

articles.title: Undersea Cables Become a Strategic Security Issue
articles.content: The latest concerns over activity near European undersea infrastructure highlight how important subsea cables have become to the global economy. These cables carry enormous volumes of internet and financial data, making their protection an increasingly important national-security issue.

articles.title: Middle East Disruption Continues to Affect Asian Energy Markets
articles.content: Asian economies remain exposed to the energy shock because many depend heavily on imported oil and gas. Higher crude prices and record tanker rates could raise transportation, manufacturing and household costs if the disruption continues.

morningSummary: Good evening. The global energy and security crisis remains at the centre of today's news. Hormuz shipping traffic has fallen to just seven vessels, while Houthi forces have expanded their control towards the Bab el-Mandeb route. Nigeria has suspended parliamentary engagements with South Africa over anti-migrant violence, while Dangote Refinery continues to strengthen its domestic crude supply. In DR Congo, the Ebola outbreak has reached a seventh province. Ukraine remains under pressure from Russian attacks, and the United States has marked 25 years since the September 11 attacks.
bigQuestion: With conflicts now affecting energy, shipping, healthcare and international relations, are the world's major powers doing enough to prevent today's crises from becoming tomorrow's global problems?
